one_sentence_story: Shepard and Metzler proved in 1971 that judging whether two angled 10-cube blocks match takes linearly longer for every extra degree — about 60 degrees per second — because your parietal and motor circuits physically simulate turning the 3D object through space.
so_what_for_you: When stuck on a complex spatial or structural puzzle, sketch it or turn a real physical model in your hands — offloading the 60-degree-per-second parietal rotation frees working memory for creative insight.
